claims.text: db/schema.sql: orders.customer_id is 'integer NOT NULL REFERENCES customers (id)' - a foreign key constraint rejecting a customer_id that doesn't exist in customers.
db/schema.sql: order_items.quantity is 'integer NOT NULL CHECK (quantity > 0)'; order_items has a composite primary key (order_id, product_id), no single-column Id.
OrderService.PlaceOrderAsync's first line is 'if (items.Count == 0) throw new ArgumentException("an order needs at least one item");', running before AddAsync or SaveChangesAsync.
PlaceOrderAsync has no explicit check for an item's quantity or productId before AddAsync/SaveChangesAsync run; those values reach the database unchecked by application code.

claims.text: PostgreSQL CHECK constraints are row-level, tested against the new/updated row on INSERT and UPDATE; PostgreSQL does not support a CHECK that references data outside the row being checked (no other rows, no other tables).

RFC 9110 section 15.3.2: a 201 response means the request has been fulfilled and has resulted in one or more new resources being created; a request that created nothing has no resource to answer 201 about.

A middleware early in the pipeline catches exceptions by type: ArgumentException becomes 400 with the exception's own Message as detail; KeyNotFoundException becomes 404; any other Exception becomes a fixed 500 'something went wrong', not that exception's message.
A POST /api/v1/orders that passes both the items.Count check and the database constraints returns 201 (OrdersController.Create ends in CreatedAtAction).
